result.response:
I have resolved the issue where `Model.objects.all().delete()` was generating a subquery `DELETE FROM table WHERE id IN (SELECT id FROM table)` instead of a direct `DELETE FROM table`.

### Cause
In `SQLDeleteCompiler.single_alias`, `sum(self.query.alias_refcount[t] > 0 for t in self.query.alias_map) == 1` was evaluated before the initial table alias was populated on new/uncompiled delete queries (where `self.query.alias_map` was empty `{}`). Because `alias_map` was empty, `single_alias` evaluated to `False` and was cached by `@cached_property`. As a result, `SQLDeleteCompiler.as_sql()` fell back to generating a subquery as if multiple table aliases were involved in the deletion.

### Solution
Updated [`SQLDeleteCompiler.single_alias`](file:///testbed/django/db/models/sql/compiler.py#L1407-L1411) in [`django/db/models/sql/compiler.py`](file:///testbed/django/db/models/sql/compiler.py) to ensure `self.query.get_initial_alias()` is called when `alias_map` has no active aliases prior to checking active alias counts.
The test suite has finished running and all tests passed. The fix is complete.
